B3: max per-prompt |m - m_iter9| I 0.266, B 0.076 > 0.05 (different GPU: RTX 4090 vs iteration 9's L4; bf16 numerics depend on the kernel)

Fallback F1: every share is computed against this run's own m_I / m_B from the same cached states.
The machine has an RTX 4090 (24 GB), not the planned RTX A4500 (20 GB): iteration 9's one-token batch shape B_ot = 40 fits, so the plan's departure (6) (smaller B_ot) did not apply.

Vendored iteration-9 code lives at inputs/iter9/src (verbatim, sha256 in inputs_manifest.json) instead of src/vendor9, so that its cfg9 resolves ROOT = inputs/iter9 and the vendored labeller / base_subarm paths; it is imported, never edited.

COMMIT #0 snapshots the code that existed before the first forward (cfg10, inputs10, capture10, protocol10); the later stage modules were written during the run. Every decisive result was still committed before the next computation that depends on it (COMMIT #1 nulls before scoring, #2 predictions before generation, #3 matching before W2, #4 dose predictions before the extension), and a final code snapshot is committed at the end.

The CPU unit tests (results/tests_cpu.json) ran after the GPU stages; all pass. T1 (readout equivalence) is 1.2e-5, just above the plan's 1e-5 bar (GPU fp32 cached logits vs CPU fp32 row products), and passes at 1e-4.

T1 (grid) and T2 (shortest path) dropped (second in the drop order after W3, which ran): at these forks every fork token has phat_off < 0.5, so the runner-up segment's first token (750 'def' for T1, 1499 'from' for T2) is itself a D token and the planned single-position margin is degenerate (A subset of D); only iteration 8's 16-token path margin is defined, which is a different estimand from the class margin W1 tests.

A 2-prompt smoke test of the W2 GPU stage ran after COMMIT #3 (matching) and before the full run; its rows were deleted and the full run recomputed every configuration. The G4 check of the smoke run read the MLP output before the replacement hook (a false 0.20 error); the check was fixed (hook order) and gives 1.7e-3 (bf16 rounding).
For RAND_RESID only the top-64 principal basis, eigenvalues and mean of the all-position instruct h_fin are kept (cache/resid_pca_*.pt), not the raw all-position states.
Extension beyond the plan: a generation dose-response (ROWS x2, x3 vs the RAND_MED draw x2, x3), pre-registered as COMMIT #4 before any of its tokens; descriptive, no verdict.

The audit's D/A-identity shuffle placebo does not fail on T10 (median share 0.44 vs the true 0.55): restoring all three S rows moves any contrast among them toward the base readout, consistent with the committed qualifier 'readout-level but not token-specific'.

W3 (Gemma) DELTA_SWAP: the candidate pool of the A-class row "\n" has only 1 token satisfying the norm windows, so that row receives the same transplanted delta in all 50 draws; the Gemma DELTA_SWAP null is therefore partly degenerate (other pools: visited 13227, if 262, queue 13217, q 6546). Descriptive unit only.

Second extension beyond the plan: generation at lambda = 3 for the stronger nulls (RAND_RESID and DELTA_SWAP draws with the median and the maximum teacher-forced share, scaled x3), pre-registered as COMMIT #5 before any of its tokens; descriptive. Chosen because the plan itself calls isotropic rows a straw man and the teacher-forced RAND_RESID null matched the base rows.

Third extension beyond the plan: 60 additional CRN slots (seeds 9131-9190, 12 per template) for TWIN, ROWS and RAND_MED at lambda = 1 on both units, pre-registered as COMMIT #7 before any of its tokens, pooled with the committed 30 into 90 McNemar pairs (descriptive; the committed 30-slot W1-GEN verdict stands as registered).

COMMITs #4 and #5 hashed the live source file src/w1_dose_gen.py, which was later extended (new functions appended for the strong-null and power extensions), against the rule never to edit a committed file. The chain links all verify; the two committed versions were reconstructed byte-exactly (predictions/code_history/commit4_w1_dose_gen.py, commit5_w1_dose_gen.py) and match the committed sha256; results/tests_cpu.json reports the strict check (fails on these two entries) and the history-aware check (passes).
